extracted.intended_audience: USPTO managers, trademark examiners and attorneys, TTAB judges, trademark stakeholders and policy makers
extracted.subtask_description: Performance standards, operational requirements, and evaluative metrics for USPTO Trademarks operations and the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB), including integrity protections, IT/analytics modernization, customer experience, pilot programs, and implementation of the Trademark Modernization Act (TMA).

rubrics_metrics.name: IT modernization & capacity investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate additional IT funding and add development teams to implement TMA requirements and increase capacity to address trademark filing surges and inventory backlogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in AI and robotic process automation (RPA) to streamline pre-examination unit business processes; continue increasing Trademarks IT modernization investment (e.g., further increases expected in FY2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative case management software for trademark fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire and deploy investigative case management software to assist trademark attorneys in tracking patterns of trademark fraud, collecting evidence, and deciding on further actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software supports the Trademarks Special Task Force for Improper Activities and helps determine when to refer matters to law enforcement or other offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use business intelligence and data analytics to guide decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand use of objective data and analytic staff (including AI/ML expertise) to drive decision-making, address application volume and fraudulent filings, and maintain register integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase staff of business intelligence analysts and expand analytic products to anticipate applicant/registrant needs and improve examination efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark dashboard products
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide management with granular insights into goods/services/classes that drive application filings and suspicious/fraudulent filings and improve identification of applicant profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dashboards are integral to strategic plan and support predictive analytics and operational decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic initiatives for trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and deploy specific analytics such as proof-of-use reporting automation, goods/services misclassification identification and automation, applicant profile analysis, growth analysis, and digitally altered specimen analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These capabilities should be expanded and integrated with AI to enhance predictive capabilities and proactively provide reliable, actionable data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting the integrity of the Trademark Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement statutory, technological, and operational adjustments to identify and address fake/digitally altered specimens, false information, and other filings that threaten the register's integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives include administrative sanctions, deletion fee, expanded letter of protest, address verification automation, and other measures described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative sanctions for improper submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner for Trademarks may investigate submissions that appear to violate Trademark Rules of Practice or USPTO website terms of use and, after notice and opportunity to respond, impose sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may include terminating proceedings; findings may be referred to Office of Enrollment and Discipline for attorney misconduct or to law enforcement for criminal conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion fee for maintenance deletions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant deletes goods or services from a registration in a maintenance declaration (years 5–6 and every 10 years), a deletion fee must be paid each time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee implemented January 2021 to disincentivize inaccurate claims of use in maintenance submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded letter of protest procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow third parties to submit relevant evidence in a pending application showing the mark is not in actual use in commerce; relevant evidence will be sent to the examining attorney for consideration of refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expansion increases third-party ability to assist examination of suspicious or non‑use claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address verification to enforce U.S. counsel rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Require domicile address from each applicant/registrant and automate address verification to evaluate invocation of the U.S. counsel rule and detect unacceptable domicile addresses designed to circumvent the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automation improves examination efficiency and reinforces compliance with representation requirements for foreign domiciliary applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMA implementation: nonuse proceedings & shortened response authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement Trademark Modernization Act provisions that establish nonuse proceedings before the Director and authorize the Director to shorten response periods to office actions, particularly for suspicious applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonuse proceedings permit third parties to challenge registrations that were never used without filing at TTAB; nonuse proceedings required to be implemented by Dec 27, 2021; other provisions as set in final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer experience (CX) program & website design standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide consistent, clear, and intuitive trademark services and redesign the Trademark basics webpages based on customer survey research, staff collaboration, and usability testing to improve accessibility for novices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure CX via satisfaction scores (example: increase from 69 to 71 among first-time visitors); track percent of customers finding pages helpful (example: 92.2% across new/redesigned pages). Use CX research findings to guide UI and communications improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CX research & usability testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct surveys on outreach/educational events and TEAS, and conduct usability testing for prototypes (e.g., identity verification) to inform improvements and ensure quality experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring customer voice into decision-making and iterate UI/communications based on findings; document CX maturity self-assessment and develop action plans as required under OMB guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Basics Boot Camp curriculum & objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver a structured eight-module virtual series for aspiring applicants covering definitions, benefits of trademarks, preparation, filing, prosecution, and maintenance requirements to reduce filing errors and unregistrable marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to educate entrepreneurs and small businesses before they use TEAS to produce more savvy trademark owners and reduce operational burdens on Trademarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law School Clinic Certification Program selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Select participating law schools based on solid IP curricula, provision of pro bono services to the public, and community networking and outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating schools enable students, under faculty supervision, to process applications before the USPTO; program expanded to prosecute matters before TTAB on appeal and oppositions, increasing pro bono assistance beyond initial prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: International cooperation via TM5
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the five largest trademark offices (TM5) to harmonize processes, discuss challenges, exchange information, and pursue cooperative projects on issues like fraudulent solicitations, bad faith, nontraditional marks, and filing trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use working-level and annual meetings to align procedures and share lessons learned; continue collaboration despite virtual meeting constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB pendency and timeliness goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims for issuance of TTAB decisions within specified timeframes: trial cases in 15 weeks or less, ex parte appeals in 12 weeks or less, and contested trial case motions in 12 weeks or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2021 actual averages: trial decisions 9.8 weeks after RFD, appeals 7.7 weeks after RFD, motions 9.9 weeks after RFD. Monitor filing surges and staff/resourcing to maintain goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited Cancellation Pilot Program evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess expedited cancellation proceedings by measuring claims distribution and default judgment rates (e.g., abandonment included in 34% of proceedings; likelihood of confusion 27%; default judgment rates: 44% overall, 49% when nonuse/abandonment included, 60% when abandonment only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pilot analysis to confirm cancellation proceedings' utility for clearing unused/abandoned marks and to inform future procedures (including preparations for TMA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery conferences & accelerated case resolution (ACR) recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend parties prepare and conduct discovery conferences constructively, seriously consider early exchanges of information/documents and ACR options during the required discussion of ACR, and reassess ACR after initial exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties invited to contact interlocutory attorney to arrange conferences to discuss stipulations and ACR that may increase proceeding efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMA ex parte expungement and reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for new ex parte cancellation expungement and ex parte reexamination proceedings allowing third parties to request cancellation of goods/services in a registration for which a mark was never used or was not used at the relevant time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These new proceedings may be faster and less expensive alternatives to contested inter partes cancellations; anticipate appeals to TTAB from Director decisions involving ex parte proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB precedential decision designation & MOP updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue precedential opinions and allow stakeholders to nominate Board decisions for precedential designation; maintain and regularly update the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board Manual of Procedure (MOP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB met its goal with 39 precedential decisions in FY2021; provide e-version and PDF of MOP and encourage stakeholder nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB Reading Room and cloud-based TTAB Center modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide enhanced public search capabilities for TTAB final decisions via Reading Room and plan a cloud-based TTAB Center to replace ESTTA, TTABVUE, and TTABIS to modernize forms, improve CX, and replace automated workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stabilize legacy systems as a foundation; phase one scheduled to replace ESTTA notice of opposition filing system and automated workflow in FY2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB fee structure adjustments & targeted partial refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust TTAB and Trademark fees to recover costs and better align fees with services; add new fees (e.g., filing an appeal brief, requesting extensions, requesting oral hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide partial refunds for petitions to cancel that result in default judgments under specific conditions (case involved only nonuse/abandonment, defendant did not appear, and no filings other than petition), creating incentives and protecting register integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and outreach expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain engagement through participation in events, roundtables, celebrations, outreach to law school clinics, and stakeholder meetings to support transparency and assistance despite virtual constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue virtual hearings with minimal interruption and provide stakeholder-facing reporting of data and performance measures (e.g., quarterly reports and TPAC meetings).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO role in AI and IP policy leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in AI-IP policy via datasets (e.g., Artificial Intelligence Patent Dataset), participation in international task forces, public reports soliciting views on AI and IP policy, and public events on AI-related IP topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use datasets and public engagement to inform policy formulation, training, and international cooperation on AI-related IP issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents 4 Partnerships platform enhancement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve the Patents 4 Partnerships online marketplace by increasing listed entries and outreach, and consider expanding or creating analogous platforms for other technology areas (e.g., green technologies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform should be searchable by extensive criteria and facilitate voluntary licensing and commercialization; outreach to industry and federal labs increases usefulness.
